title: Collatz basin densities, Fourier decay, and Syracuse integrability: papers and Lean proofs
description:
Three papers by Lucas Valbuena with Lean sources and recorded verification. Quadratic cylinder energy and integrability of the Syracuse law proves an upper bound 24k+8k² for the full-Haar energy of the depth-k fair Syracuse cylinder density, for k≥1, and a normalized stationary density whose exact real Lp range is 1≤p<2. The argument credits Tao's law, fine-scale mixing and offset injectivity.

Fourier decay for truncated Syracuse affine laws proves primitive Fourier decay uniform in a growing conductor deficit and affine seed, with conditional decay on polynomial-mass total-exponent slices and the central slice. Constants are ineffective, and no conductor-power bound at fixed positive deficit ratio is claimed.

Collatz basin densities and canonical traces from first-passage stabilization proves uniform inverse-linear predecessor density bounds, including periodic targets, using the credited work of Mazur and Said Duran. The inverse-linear form was proposed by Wirsching. Further results include a finite-energy criterion equivalent to universal eventual periodicity, a raw occupation lower bound and conditional divergent excess, and an almost-sure inverse height clock.

The archive includes the papers, LaTeX sources, theorem maps, pinned dependencies and proof verification records. Each bundle distinguishes fresh strict compilation and individual kernel replay from authenticated reuse of external libraries. Audited results use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The sharp-integrability bundle freshly compiled and individually kernel checked all 362 internal sources and their complete declaration audit, with 726 successful commands and 10,465 audited module/constant rows. External compiled libraries were fingerprinted and reused; their full source closures were not rebuilt. Setup reuse and record verification in fresh processes and a relocated directory also passed. The fresh dependency-download branch was not exercised.

These results do not prove the Collatz conjecture. Sublinear masked energy, additional cycles, and a matching raw occupation upper bound remain unresolved. No exhaustive priority claim is made. Original code and documentation use MIT; imported and adapted formal sources retain their own licenses and notices. The papers and LaTeX sources use CC BY 4.0. Automated proof development and review are disclosed and do not constitute external peer review. Earlier standalone papers remain in repository history and prior releases.
